Zhou Qiu was a native of Xiapi, a fugitive in Wu, a wine-seller of bad conduct; the king despised him and would not employ him.
Zhou Qiu was a native of Xiapi, a fugitive in Wu, and a wine-seller of bad conduct; the king despised him and would not employ him.
酤酒 identifies Zhou Qiu as a wine-seller, not a hard-drinking wastrel.
Zhou Qiu of Xiapi was a fugitive in Wu, a hard-drinking wastrel whom the king despised and would not employ.
Zhou Qiu of Xiapi was a fugitive in Wu and a disreputable wine-seller whom the king despised and would not employ.
酤酒 identifies Zhou Qiu as a wine-seller, not a hard-drinking wastrel.
Zhou Qiu then presented himself and said to the king, “Because I lack ability I have not been employed among the ranks.
Zhou Qiu then requested an audience and said to the king, “Because I lack ability I have not been employed among the ranks.
上謁 means requesting an audience, not forcing one.
He forced an audience: “For my faults I have no place in the ranks.
He requested an audience and said, “Because I lack ability, I have been given no place in the ranks.
上謁 means requesting an audience, not forcing one.
He reached the relay station, summoned the magistrate inside the gate, and had his followers execute the magistrate on a fabricated charge.
He reached the relay station, summoned the magistrate into his room, and had his followers execute him on a fabricated charge.
戶 is the room or quarters at the relay station, not a city gate.
At the post-house he called the magistrate in and had his men cut him down on a trumped charge.
At the post-house he summoned the magistrate into his room and had his men cut him down on a trumped-up charge.
戶 is the room or quarters at the relay station, not a city gate.
He then gathered his brothers' trusted bold officers and told them, “Wu rebel troops will soon arrive; they will sack Xiapi in less than the time of a meal.

He then summoned his brothers and the influential local officers with whom he was friendly and told them, “Wu's rebel troops will soon arrive; they will massacre Xiapi in less than the time of a meal.
昆弟所善豪吏 means his brothers and influential local officers known to him, not bold kinsmen.
He rallied bold kinsmen: “Wu’s host is coming; they will level Xiapi before a meal cools.
He summoned his brothers and the influential local officers he knew: “Wu’s rebel army is coming; it will massacre Xiapi in less than the time of a meal.
昆弟所善豪吏 means his brothers and influential local officers known to him, not bold kinsmen.

The August Emperor Gaozu personally left merit and virtue, establishing the princes; Kings You of Zhao and Daohui of Qi had no posterity; Emperor Xiaowen took pity and added grace, enfeoffing King You's son Sui and Daohui's son Ang and others, ordering them to maintain their ancestors' temples as Han's outer bulwarks—virtue matching Heaven and Earth, brightness joining sun and moon.

The August Emperor Gaozu personally bestowed merit and virtue by establishing the princes. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off without successors, Emperor Xiaowen took pity and extended his grace, making King You's son Sui, King Daohui's son Ang, and others kings so that they could maintain their forefathers' ancestral temples and serve as Han's outer bulwarks—his virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.
絕無後 says the royal lines had been cut off, not that both kings personally died without heirs.

Gaozu set up the kingdoms; when You of Zhao and Daohui of Qi died without heirs, Xiaowen raised Sui, Ang, and the rest to tend their shrines as Han’s shield—his kindness spanned heaven and earth and shone like the luminaries.

Gaozu established the kingdoms. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off, Emperor Wen compassionately made You’s son Sui, Daohui’s son Ang, and others kings so that they could tend their forefathers’ shrines and serve as Han’s outer bulwarks. His virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.
絕無後 says the royal lines had been cut off, not that both kings personally died without heirs.

Yet the King of Wu Liu Bi turned his back on virtue and violated righteousness, enticed and harbored fugitive criminals from the realm, threw the realm's currency into confusion, and for twenty years claimed illness and did not attend court.

Yet the King of Wu Liu Bi turned his back on virtue and violated righteousness, enticed and harbored fugitive criminals from the realm, threw the realm's currency into confusion, and for more than twenty years claimed illness and did not attend court.
稱疾不朝 describes claiming illness and remaining away from court for twenty years, not feigning sickness at court.
Yet Liu Bi spurned right, drew runaways, debased the coinage, and feigned sickness twenty years at court.
Yet Liu Bi spurned virtue, drew in fugitives, disrupted the currency, and for more than twenty years pleaded illness and stayed away from court.
稱疾不朝 describes claiming illness and remaining away from court for twenty years, not feigning sickness at court.

Now he has joined with King Wu of Chu, Liu Wu, King Zhao Sui, King Jiaoxi Ang, King Jinan Pi Guang, King Zichuan Xian, and King Jiaodong Xiongqü in vertical alliance to plot rebellion—unprincipled and lawless—raised troops to endanger the ancestral temples, murdered great ministers and Han envoys, coerced the myriad people, slaughtered the innocent, burned and destroyed commoners' homes, exhumed their tombs—utterly cruel and violent.

Now he has joined with Liu Wu, king of Chu, Liu Sui, king of Zhao, Liu Ang, king of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang, king of Jinan, Liu Xian, king of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu, king of Jiaodong, in an alliance to plot rebellion. Lawless in their treason, they raised troops to endanger the ancestral temples, murdered great ministers and Han envoys, coerced the people, slaughtered the innocent, burned commoners' homes, and dug open their tombs—utterly cruel and violent.
The rebel kings require their full Liu names and normalized Piguang spelling for consistent identity linking.

Now he leagues with Liu Wu, king of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, Pi Guang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqü of Jiaodong—lawless traitors who menace the temples, butcher ministers and envoys, dragoon the people, kill the guiltless, burn homes, and open graves—monstrous cruelty.

Now he has allied with Liu Wu of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong to plot rebellion. These lawless traitors menace the temples, murder ministers and envoys, coerce the people, kill the innocent, burn their homes, and dig open their graves. Their cruelty is monstrous.
The rebel kings require their full Liu names and normalized Piguang spelling for consistent identity linking.
Those who strike rebels shall take deep advance and heavy killing as merit; all rebel leaders beheaded or captured who rank at three hundred piculs or above shall be put to death without sparing.
Those who strike the rebels shall take deep advances and heavy killing as merit; every captured rebel of the three-hundred-picul rank or above shall be put to death, with none spared.
The execution order applies to captured rebels of three-hundred-picul rank or above.
Pursue deep and kill hard for merit; every rebel chief of three hundred piculs or higher whom you take—execute; grant no quarter.
Advance deep and kill many to earn merit; execute every captured rebel of three-hundred-picul rank or higher, sparing none.
The execution order applies to captured rebels of three-hundred-picul rank or above.
Liang then made Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, brother of the minister who died for Chu, generals, and only then were they able to inflict some defeats on the Wu army.
Liang then made Han Anguo and Zhang Yu, younger brother of Chu's chancellor who had died in service, generals; only then were they able to inflict some defeats on the Wu army.
張羽 is the younger brother of Chu’s chancellor who died in service, not the dead chancellor himself.
Only when Liang raised Han Anguo and Zhang Yu—brother of Chu’s martyr minister—as generals could they begin to bloody Wu’s advance.
Only when Liang made Han Anguo and Zhang Yu—the younger brother of Chu’s chancellor, who had died in service—generals could it begin to defeat Wu’s troops.
張羽 is the younger brother of Chu’s chancellor who died in service, not the dead chancellor himself.
The Wu army wished to go west, but Liang defended its cities and they dared not advance west; they therefore turned toward Zhou Yafu’s army and offered battle at Xiayi.
The Wu army wished to go west, but Liang defended its cities and they dared not advance; they therefore turned toward Zhou Yafu’s army and met it at Xiayi.
會下邑 means meeting at Xiayi, not below the city.
Wu meant to drive west, yet Liang’s walls blocked the way; they dared not push on and veered toward Zhou Yafu’s camp, meeting him below Xiayi.
Wu meant to drive west, but Liang held its cities and blocked the way. The rebels dared not push on, so they turned toward Zhou Yafu’s army and met it at Xiayi.
會下邑 means meeting at Xiayi, not below the city.
Wu’s grain was cut off; the soldiers starved. They repeatedly challenged to battle, then by night rushed Zhou Yafu’s ramparts, striking the southeast.
Wu’s grain was cut off and its soldiers starved. They repeatedly challenged to battle, then rushed Zhou Yafu’s ramparts by night, making a feint against the southeast.
驚東南 is a feint against the southeast before the actual northwest attack.
With supplies gone and men famished, Wu taunted day after day, then stormed the southeast corner of Yafu’s lines by night.
With supplies gone and the men starving, Wu repeatedly challenged Yafu to battle, then rushed his ramparts by night and feinted against the southeast.
驚東南 is a feint against the southeast before the actual northwest attack.
The King of Wu then fled by night with a thousand picked warriors of his personal guard, crossed the Huai, made his way to Dantu, and took refuge with Eastern Yue.
The King of Wu then fled by night with a thousand picked warriors from under his banner, crossed the Huai, made his way to Dantu, and took refuge with Eastern Yue.
戲下壯士 are picked warriors under Liu Bi’s banner, not necessarily household guards.
Liu Bi slipped away at the head of a thousand household guards, crossed the Huai, made for Dantu, and threw himself on Eastern Yue.
Liu Bi slipped away at night with a thousand picked warriors from under his banner, crossed the Huai, made for Dantu, and took refuge with Eastern Yue.
戲下壯士 are picked warriors under Liu Bi’s banner, not necessarily household guards.
Eastern Yue had perhaps more than ten thousand troops and sent men to gather scattered fugitives.
Eastern Yue had perhaps more than ten thousand troops, and Liu Bi sent men to gather his scattered soldiers.
Liu Bi sent agents to regather his own scattered soldiers; Eastern Yue is not the subject.
Eastern Yue could field more than ten thousand men and began rounding up Wu stragglers.
Eastern Yue could field more than ten thousand men, and Liu Bi sent agents to gather the remnants of his army.
Liu Bi sent agents to regather his own scattered soldiers; Eastern Yue is not the subject.

Han sent men to tempt Eastern Yue with profit; Eastern Yue then deceived the King of Wu. When the King of Wu came out to review the troops, they had him speared to death, placed his head in a box, and galloped the relay post to report.

Han sent men to tempt Eastern Yue with rewards, and Eastern Yue then deceived the King of Wu. When he came out to comfort and reward the troops, they had him speared to death, placed his head in a container, and sent it by relay to report the news.
出勞軍 means coming out to comfort and reward or address the troops, not reviewing their ranks.

Han general Marquis of Gonggao, Huidang, sent the king a letter saying, “By edict We punish the unrighteous; those who surrender shall be pardoned, their crimes removed, and their former status restored;

Han general Han Tuidang, marquis of Gonggao, sent the king a letter saying, “By edict We punish the unrighteous; those who surrender shall be pardoned, their crimes removed, and their former status restored;
頹當 is Han Tuidang; the previous Huidang spelling was inconsistent with the same man elsewhere in the corpus.
Huidang of Gonggao wrote: “The throne punishes treason; yield and you are forgiven, your guilt wiped, your old rank returned;
Han Tuidang, marquis of Gonggao, wrote: “The throne punishes treason; yield and you are forgiven, your guilt wiped away, and your former standing restored;
頹當 is Han Tuidang; the previous Huidang spelling was inconsistent with the same man elsewhere in the corpus.
Marquis of Gonggao, holding drum and gong, received him and said, “The king has suffered in military affairs; I wish to hear how the king raised troops.”
The marquis of Gonggao, holding the gong and drum that symbolized military command, received him and said, “The king has suffered through military affairs; I wish to hear how the king raised troops.”
金鼓 are the gong and drum emblems of military command, not a drum and mallet.
Huidang, drum and mallet in hand, asked, “You have borne the war—tell me how you came to arms.”
Han Tuidang received him holding the gong and drum of command and said, “You have suffered through this war; tell me how you came to raise troops.”
金鼓 are the gong and drum emblems of military command, not a drum and mallet.
General Li attacked Zhao; in the tenth month he took it, and the King of Zhao committed suicide.
General Li attacked Zhao and took it after ten months; the King of Zhao committed suicide.
十月而下之 means Zhao fell after a ten-month campaign, not specifically in the tenth month.
Li Ji stormed Zhao in the tenth month; King Zhao killed himself.
General Li took Zhao after a ten-month campaign, and the king of Zhao killed himself.
十月而下之 means Zhao fell after a ten-month campaign, not specifically in the tenth month.

The appraisal says: The king of Jing was made king because, when Han was first settled and the realm not yet gathered, even though he was a distant kinsman, by policy he was made king to hold the ground between the Yangzi and the Huai.

The appraisal says: The king of Jing was made king because, when Han had only just been settled and the realm was not yet united, policy called for even this distant kinsman to be made king and hold the region between the Yangzi and Huai.
The historian’s appraisal is a direct policy judgment; the prior chess-piece image was invented.
Ban Gu’s verdict: Jing was enfeoffed while the dynasty was still raw—distant blood, yet a deliberate chess piece to anchor the Huai–Yangzi belt.
The appraisal says: When Han had only just been settled and the realm was not yet united, policy called for even this distant kinsman to be made king and hold the region between the Yangzi and Huai.
The historian’s appraisal is a direct policy judgment; the prior chess-piece image was invented.
Liu Ze rose through Tian Sheng, who by stratagem stirred the Lü clan, yet in the end faced south as solitary ruler for three generations.
Liu Ze rose through Tian Sheng, whose expedient spurred the Lü clan into action; his line nevertheless sat facing south and styled themselves sovereign for three generations.
南面稱孤 means Liu Ze’s line ruled as kings for three generations.
Liu Ze climbed on Tian Sheng’s intrigues against the Lüs, yet his line faced the throne for three reigns.
Liu Ze rose through Tian Sheng, whose stratagem spurred the Lü clan into action; his line nevertheless ruled as kings for three generations.
南面稱孤 means Liu Ze’s line ruled as kings for three generations.
‘Do not be the first to seize power, or you will bear its blame’—does this not speak of Chao Cuo!
‘Do not be the first to devise the stratagem, or you will bear its blame’—does this not speak of Chao Cuo?
